root_motivation: A tenant that hits a free-plan limit is told only the number it exceeded: budget_exceeded/quota_exceeded refusals say "500 exceeds plan's 500" and stop (src/errors.rs:690, src/budget.rs:237) -- no checkout_url/upgrade field exists anywhere (git grep checkout_url empty). An agent reading that has no tool name, no plan, no reset time, so it either retries until midnight or tells its human "it failed". When a payment does happen, the webhook never stamps paid_unix live (only a one-time migration backfill from plan_since exists), so the funnel's paid stage stays invisible and unattributed to which refusal earned it; the market test's one assumed leaf (a refusal with a next step converts at all) is unmeasurable. Fix: every plan/budget refusal carries next:{tool,plan,why,resets_at}; checkout(source) tags the Stripe session; the webhook stamps paid_unix/paid_test_unix by mode; billing.status returns a receipt; admin.funnel/admin.upgrades report by trigger.
user_persona: Four (PRD user stories): the agent whose 501st call returns next.tool=billing.checkout/why/resets_at, calls checkout(source) and hands the URL to its human with instructions; the human who pays and sees billing.status's receipt (plan, amount, paid_at, invoice_ref); Operator Joe, whose admin.funnel shows paid 3 and upgrades_by_trigger by limit; the self-hosting agent on a billing-off host, whose refusal says next.tool is null, so it waits instead of looping.

additional.next_off_mode_lives_in_the_message_not_a: AC1's next is exactly {tool,plan,why,resets_at} (no fifth key); AC2 says 'the text says billing is not enabled on this host' without naming a next subfield for it, so that sentence was read as the refusal's own outer message (already operator-authored prose per every other Structured error in this crate), not a new key inside next -- next itself stays the same 4-key shape in both modes, only tool flips to null.
additional.invoice_ref_reuses_tenant_billing_ref_no: requirement 4 names invoice_ref alongside plan/amount_cents/currency/paid_at/mode on the receipt, but the PRD's own migration section lists only billing_events.source and tenants.paid_test_unix as new columns. tenant.billing_ref (the Stripe customer/subscription id, already loaded on every billing.status call) is exactly 'a reference a human could match against their Stripe receipt' and needs no schema change, so the receipt's invoice_ref is that field, not a new billing_events column.
additional.session_id_added_beyond_the_named_migrat: AC7 (admin.upgrades) needs to pair a 'checkout started' moment with its eventual completion/expiry, but the PRD names no persisted checkout-attempts table and no session-id column. billing_events already gets a schema touch for source (named); adding session_id to the SAME migration (rather than a second one) is the minimal extension that lets a self-ledgered checkout.started row (written by billing::checkout at session-creation time, never on a P1 AC13 cache-hit reuse) correlate with the webhook's own checkout.session.completed row by Stripe's own session id -- no new table.
additional.checkout_source_allowlist_is_every_limit: requirement 2 says source is validated against 'the refusal codes plus manual' -- read as the limit_name/dimension identifiers next_upgrade's five sites each put in their own why (calls_per_day/tools_max/secrets_max from the three plan-limit sites, max_child_calls/max_est_tokens/max_tool_latency_ms/max_wall_ms from budget_ceiling_exceeded's field keys, child_calls/est_tokens/tool_latency_ms/wall_ms from budget_exceeded's dimensions), not the AppError `code` field (which is just 'quota_exceeded' for all three plan-limit sites and so can't disambiguate which limit).
additional.admin_funnel_paid_3_is_the_pre_existing_: AC6 says 'paid 3 and upgrades_by_trigger {...}'; activation-funnel's own FUNNEL_STAGES already includes a 'paid' stage (count from paid_unix) in admin.funnel's stages array, so once this PRD's webhook actually stamps paid_unix that stage already reads 3 with zero new code -- only upgrades_by_trigger (grouped by billing_events.source) is new.
additional.budget_ceiling_exceeded_and_budget_excee: requirement 1 (P0) names all five refusal sites (the three plan-limit ones plus budget_ceiling_exceeded and budget_exceeded) as carrying next, but only AC1/AC2 are testable against a concrete scenario (both calls_per_day-shaped); the other two are built (resolve_and_validate takes &AppState, BudgetTracker gains a plan field) in their own non-AC commit per the dispatch's own 'one commit per requirement with no AC of its own' rule, proven by the pre-existing budget_ac* suite staying green rather than a new upgrade_ac* file.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does a refusal with a next step matter if there is no paying traffic yet?
five_whys_trace.a: This is the funnel's last stage being wired before the first wave (PRD grounding: 'not failure'); PRD-grand-loop-billing's own goal 4 (next: billing.checkout on quota refusals) was drafted but never built, so the very first real conversion would already be invisible without this PRD.

five_whys_trace.q: Why is a refusal with no next step a problem for an agent specifically, not just a human?
five_whys_trace.a: An agent has no UI to discover billing.checkout exists -- it only ever sees the tool list it was given and the error payload in front of it; without next.tool in that payload it has no path from 'quota_exceeded' to 'call billing.checkout', so it retries the same call until the day rolls over or reports failure upward.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does paid_unix staying null matter if plan already flips to pro on checkout?
five_whys_trace.a: plan flipping is enough to unlock the tenant, but PRD-mcphost-activation-funnel's own FUNNEL_STAGES array already has a 'paid' stage reading paid_unix -- with nothing stamping it live (only a one-time migration backfill from plan_since), every NEW paid tenant after that migration ran is invisible to admin.funnel/healthz, breaking the exact stage the market test was built to watch.

five_whys_trace.q: Why can't the funnel say which refusal earned a conversion today?
five_whys_trace.a: billing_events (migration 0006) carries event_type/plan/amount/mode but no source -- the webhook has always applied a checkout.session.completed event without ever reading back which limit the tenant's own checkout() call was started in response to, because checkout() itself never recorded or forwarded that context to Stripe or the ledger.

five_whys_trace.q: Why wasn't this wired when the billing rails themselves (grand-loop-billing) shipped?
five_whys_trace.a: grand-loop-billing's own scope was proving a real $19 payment end-to-end (checkout session, webhook, ledger) -- it explicitly deferred the 'next step' UX and per-refusal attribution as goal 4, and nothing since has revisited the refusal/attribution half until Joe's market test needed to measure conversion by trigger.

ambiguities_resolved.question: When billing is off, does next keep a plan field (the catalog still has a next plan up), or does it drop to just {tool: null, why, resets_at}?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Kept: requirement 1 defines plan as a general rule (next plan up per plans.rs) and only calls out tool/the message text as the billing-off override, so plan stays populated even when tool is null -- an operator reading the refusal still learns what plan would unlock the limit, even on a host with no Stripe key.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Does a P1 AC13 cache-hit checkout (the same open session reused for a second billing.checkout call) get its own checkout.started row for admin.upgrades?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: No -- it is the same Stripe session, not a new attempt; only the branch that actually calls BillingClient::create_checkout_session self-ledgers checkout.started, so admin.upgrades never double-counts a tenant polling billing.checkout before its first session expires.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Does the funnel's upgrades_by_trigger (AC6) count every paid tenant host-wide, or only those inside admin.funnel's own days/source_class/signup_source/invited filters?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Scoped to the same filtered rows stages already reports over (via a new FunnelRow.paid_source field populated by a correlated subquery) -- consistent with every other field admin.funnel already returns, and what the AC6 test (three tenants paid "now", well inside the default 7-day window) exercises.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Does apply_checkout_completed's existing plan-upgrade behavior (upgrade_tenant_plan fires regardless of live/test mode, proven by the pre-existing billing_ac06 test with livemode:false) change under this PRD?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: No -- only the NEW paid_unix/paid_test_unix stamps are mode-gated; the pre-existing plan flip stays unconditional (a self-hoster's test-mode trial checkout still unlocks pro), since billing_ac06 already pins that behavior and the PRD's own guardrail (test-mode checkout never counts as paid) is about the funnel's paid_unix signal specifically, not plan access.
